# Independent ACL edge oracle

`edge-cases.zip` retains 96 additional synthetic cases, each with the exact
upstream compressor's `.acl` output and the matching upstream C++ decompressor's
`.csv` samples. These are independent expected values, not samples generated by
the Rust implementation. The archive is about 0.65 MiB and expands to less than
2 MiB. It is only read by a Rust regression test; no extraction or network access
is needed.

The sources are Animation Compression Library **v2.1.0**, commit
`414689d5cff4286a7898487a46dc5e48005d38da`, and its RTM submodule at
`d7982f2b2524feeb322f424b29cf43df30b5d5b7`. Both are MIT licensed; the exact
notices are retained beside these fixtures in `LICENSE-ACL` and `LICENSE-RTM`.
`edge_oracle.cpp` adapts the existing `oracle.cpp` generator under this
repository's MIT license. It uses upstream public APIs; Cargo never compiles or
links C++, and the application has no ACL or C++ runtime dependency.

The Cartesian case matrix is:

| Parameter | Values |
| --- | --- |
| Transform tracks | 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 15, 16, 17 |
| Source frames | 1, 11, 37 |
| Format 0 | Variable rotation and vectors |
| Format 1 | Full precision rotation and vectors |
| Format 2 | Full precision dropped-W quaternion; variable vectors |
| Format 3 | Variable rotation and vectors, with every scale set to identity |

This covers all-default and all-constant clips, one-frame clips, partial groups
of four rotations, the packed 16-track boundary, dropped-W full precision, and
omitted scale data. Upstream loop optimization can remove a repeated endpoint,
so `source_frames` in a filename can exceed `stored_frames` in the ACL/CSV.
The Rust API returns the stored samples and preserves the loop flag.

The first CSV row is `tracks,stored_frames,10,sample_rate`. Subsequent rows are
frame-major quaternion XYZW, translation XYZ, and scale XYZ for each track.
`manifest.json` inside the ZIP records both pinned upstream revisions, the
generator's SHA-256, dimensions, format, and exact SHA-256 of every ACL/CSV pair.
Tests compare every scalar against the independently decoded CSV, with a
relative tolerance of `2e-6` and an absolute floor of `2e-6`.

To reproduce with those upstream checkouts and their RTM submodule:

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/assetstudio-acl-edges
g++ -std=c++14 -O2 -I "$ACL_SRC/includes" -I "$ACL_SRC/external/rtm/includes" \
    edge_oracle.cpp -o /tmp/assetstudio-acl-edge-oracle
/tmp/assetstudio-acl-edge-oracle /tmp/assetstudio-acl-edges
python3 pack_edges.py /tmp/assetstudio-acl-edges edge-cases.zip
cargo test -p unity-rs-core --test acl_edge_oracle --locked
```

The committed data was generated on Linux x86-64 with GCC 13.3.0 and upstream
RTM's default SIMD path; packing used Python 3.12.14 and zlib 1.3.2.
The packer sorts entries, fixes timestamps and permissions,
and records no absolute paths. Repeated runs with the same inputs and zlib build
are byte-identical; compiler floating-point settings and zlib versions can change
generated CSV rounding or compressed ZIP bytes. The manifest hashes identify the
exact committed upstream outputs; the Rust regression uses the stated numeric
tolerance across platforms.
